create.name: Sydney Zen Centre
create.bio:
The Sydney Zen Centre describes itself as Australia's original Zen Buddhist community. It is a lay sangha in the Diamond Sangha lineage, whose founder Robert Aitken Rōshi first came to Sydney in 1979 and led yearly sesshin there for almost a decade; John Tarrant, one of his heirs, also led early retreats. Today a circle of teachers guides the community with an elected board, led by Subhana Barzaghi Rōshi and Gillian Coote Rōshi with Will Moon, Maggie Gluek and Jane Andino, and Peter Bursky, an apprentice teacher since 2019, is due to receive transmission in December 2026.

The centre has two zendos. In the inner-west suburb of Annandale a former corner shop serves as the city zendo, used for evening sittings on Mondays and Wednesdays, a monthly Sunday zazenkai, ceremonies on the full moon and non-residential sesshin, with teacher interviews during sittings; online groups meet on Tuesday mornings and Thursday evenings. Kodoji, its bush zendo, sits in a valley below the sandstone cliffs of Yengo National Park, about two hours north-west of the city near St Albans. Members bought the land in 1984 and built it up over years of work weekends, and it hosts the longer residential retreats. Newcomers start with a monthly orientation evening, and recent talks are published as a podcast.

courses.title: Orientation for newcomers
courses.description: A relaxed monthly Tuesday evening at the Annandale zendo, or on Zoom, with instruction in sitting and walking meditation and an introduction to Zen ideas and forms. Places are booked by email with the volunteer named for each date, and the fee also covers one further sitting.
courses.price: There is a $20 fee which covers the Orientation night and one other sitting night

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin 2026
courses.description: A non-residential sesshin at the Annandale zendo marking the Buddha's awakening, led jointly by Allan Marett Rōshi and Peter Bursky, with zazen, walking meditation, chanting, interviews and talks. People can attend full-time or choose blocks of sitting; it closes with Peter Bursky's transmission ceremony.
courses.price: Full-time: SZC member $400, non-member $470; Part-time: SZC member $22 per block, non-member $26 per block

courses.title: Zazenkai
courses.description: A monthly Sunday half-day of extended sitting at the city zendo with a dharma talk, a sutra service and interviews with a teacher; some months are given to ceremonies, a creative-arts workshop or a bushwalking retreat. An orientation is needed first.

courses.title: Women's retreat at Kodoji
courses.description: A weekend at the bush zendo for women with meditation experience, sitting, walking and sharing meals together in the valley, with simple camping or dormitory beds.

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: Membership supports the teachers and both zendos and gives free entry to regular events, private interviews with teachers, retreat discounts and use of Kodoji. Standard, concession and online-only rates are suggested.
courses.price: Standard: Annual: $575; Limited engagement/Concession: Annual: $315; Online only: Annual: $150

free_resources.title: Sydney Zen Centre podcasts
free_resources.description: Recordings of teisho and dharma talks from the centre's teachers and senior students, often working through a classic koan, posted soon after they are given.

free_resources.title: Sutras
free_resources.description: The texts the sangha chants at its services, available to read on its website.
